title: Character Model — Propp Role × Greimas Actant × Archetype
source: authored synthesis for monomyth (Propp 1928 × Greimas 1966 × Jung/Vogler)
tier_note: The cross-cutting character model: each dramatic role is a typical alignment across three orthogonal facets. These are PRIORS, not laws — archetypes float (a Shapeshifter can take the Helper or Opponent actant). A generated character selects one alignment as its spine, then may bend facets for twists.

items.name: Protagonist
items.description: The seeker/victim hero who desires the object and benefits from winning it.

items.name: Antagonist
items.description: The villain who opposes the subject; embodies the shadow to be defeated or integrated.

items.name: Guide
items.description: The donor who tests the hero and bestows the crucial agent or knowledge.

items.name: Companion
items.description: The helper who accompanies and aids; may carry the trickster's disruptive edge.

items.name: Prize
items.description: The sought-for person/object; often ambiguous in loyalty, hence a shapeshifter.

items.name: Quest-Giver
items.description: The dispatcher who makes the lack known and sends the hero off — the herald of change.

items.name: Pretender
items.description: The false hero who claims the hero's deeds; a secondary shadow/trickster, later exposed.

items.name: Gatekeeper
items.description: The threshold guardian — no dedicated Propp role; surfaces as the donor's test or a minor opponent barring passage between worlds.
